versions.name: RXV2-0.9.638-usb-wording
versions.notes: Help on In-flight adjustments and Command line: the USB cable runs from the dongle to the flight controller, not to a laptop (Malcolm: some might assume it needs the laptop). Includes 0.9.637.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.637-help-try
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments help (Malcolm): after the boxes fill with the current value, change one or two to the values you want to try and leave the first box as it is, so a flick of the switch takes you back. Includes 0.9.636.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.636-help
versions.notes: Help screens: the In-flight adjustments and Command line pages now have the ? button (they were the only pages without it) with short, step-ordered help - setting one up, Switch, Knob, Banks, Numbers, USB; commands, leaving, what is paused. Includes 0.9.635.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.635-prefill
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments: choosing a setting (or adding a line) fills the value boxes with that setting's current value in that bank, ready to edit (Malcolm 2026-09-11). The page reads the bank over USB and puts the bank in use back straight away. Every rates, PID, PID+, rescue and governor-profile adjustment is readable; the four global ones (governor idle/auto throttle, accelerometer trims) stay blank. Includes 0.9.634.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.634-rate-units
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments: the Rate entries now show and save the same numbers as the Rates page (Rotorflight stores Rate/5 for its own rates type, Rate/10 for the older types; the page reads the rates type from the flight controller and converts both ways). Rates entries renamed: 'Pitch rate curve shape (Shape)', 'Pitch top rotation speed (Rate)', 'Pitch expo'. Includes 0.9.633.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.633-no-bank-lines
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments: the bank-switch lines (PID bank / rates bank selector) are no longer shown or offered here - the Switches page owns them (Malcolm: 'this is defined in another area'). They stay untouched on the flight controller and still tell this page which channel range means bank 1 to 4. No '(nothing)' entry; a new line starts as 'Pitch P gain in bank 1'. Includes 0.9.632.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.632-short-list
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments: by default the list offers only PIDs and rates, each per bank ('Yaw P gain in bank 1'); a 'Show every setting' switch reveals the full Rotorflight set (over 400 entries, including 'in the bank in use'). The bank-switch entries read 'PID bank switch (1 to 4)' / 'Rates bank switch (1 to 4)'. Includes 0.9.631.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.631-bank-list
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments: the 'What it changes' list itself now offers every setting per bank - 'Yaw P gain in bank 1', 'in bank 2' ... and 'in the bank in use' - grouped by bank; no separate bank choice. Garbled labels fixed (collective, cutoff, altitude). Includes 0.9.630.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.630-in-bank
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments: a line now reads as one phrase, 'Yaw P gain in bank 1', with the bank chosen right beside the setting (bank 1 to 4, or the bank in use) - Malcolm 2026-09-11: 'otherwise it is still much too vague'. Includes 0.9.629.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.629-only-in-bank
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments: each line can say 'Only in bank N' - it then works only while your bank switch has that bank in use, so a knob or a switch can carry values that suit one bank, and another line can serve another (Malcolm 2026-09-11: '40 and 60 might make sense in bank 3 but in bank 1 they would be far too low'). The bank's switch positions are read off your own PID-bank line. Includes 0.9.628.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.628-bank-in-use
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments: the bank settings read 'PID bank in use (1 to 4)' and 'Rates bank in use (1 to 4)' - the value is the bank number (Malcolm 2026-09-11: 'which bank flies - what does that mean?'). Includes 0.9.627.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.627-adj-help
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments: the help screen rewritten - clear and short (Malcolm 2026-09-11). Includes 0.9.626.
